Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear asks. Short summary below and I've attached a CSV with our current subprocessor inventory and a one-pager that outlines routes. If you want a formal evidence pack we can add timestamps/log extracts.

1) Regions & runtime hops (hosted):
- Primary processing occurs in the region you choose at project creation (us-west-2, us-east-1, eu-west-1 are common).
- If capacity or model compatibility requires it, requests may be routed to a compatible variant in a secondary region within the same commercial geography (e.g., us-west-2 -> us-east-1).
- We never route into a different legal jurisdiction without customer consent; default hosted behavior keeps data within the selected geography (US, EU, APAC).

2) Subprocessor brief:
- Core compute: our dedicated cloud partners (list attached).
- Storage/cache: ephemeral KV caches are in-region; long-term logs/metrics are aggregated to our analytics partner (see CSV).
- Security/monitoring vendors: receive aggregated telemetry only; no customer prompt text.

3) Deletion timeline and handoffs:
- Customer request received -> immediate soft-delete marker in control plane (T+0).
- Indexes and cached prefixes are purged asynchronously (T+0 to T+minutes).
- Full deletion from backups and aggregated analytics: typically completed within 30 days; we provide attestations at completion.
- If subprocessors require explicit notification, we coordinate and include them in the attestation; that step can extend completion to 45 days in rare cases.

Attachments: redwood-subprocessors-2027.csv, data-residency-overview-2027.pdf

Next steps: if you have jurisdictional constraints (e.g., no cross-border hops even within a geography) we can lock routing to a single AZ/region and provide a confined plan.

Regards,

Hi Sarah — quick clarifications:

1) Raw prompt text: Only the serving runtime and our in-region ephemeral caches have access to raw prompt text. Subprocessors that run customer-dedicated compute may see prompts if they host the dedicated GPU pool (listed in the CSV). Our monitoring/analytics stack receives hashed/aggregated telemetry by default — we do not ship raw prompts to analytics partners except under customer-approved debugging sessions (consent-driven).

2) Cross-region analytics: We run asynchronous aggregated metrics across regions for capacity planning; these are numeric aggregates (latency, token counts). Raw prompt text is not replicated across regions for analytics.

3) Deletion API example (snippet):
POST /v1/projects/{proj_id}/data/delete
Headers: Authorization: Bearer <token>
Body: {"scope":"prompts","keys":["user_abc123","session_987"]} 
Response: {"request_id":"req_...","status":"pending","expected_completion":"30d"}

For customers requiring faster guarantees we offer an SLA-backed private deployment option that can push the backup/window down to 7 days — if NovaMed needs that we can scope it.

Marissa — FYI in case we want to offer an evidence bundle for their procurement packet.

Best,
